text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bund futures were higher in late trade after spending the day drifting in a 22 basis point range influenced mostly by the U.S. market. With few domestic events emerging that could have left an impact on the market, Bund traders looked to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to the U.S. senate to provide the market with direction. But by late in the day, Greenspan had not mentioned economic conditions.
The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.17, up 0.14 from Wednesday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - UK gilt futures closed up on Thursday but off their highs as they struggled to build on gains made after a successful five-year gilt auction.
The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-5/32, up 6/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.
FRANCE - French PIBOR interest rate futures finished Matif trading firmer, lifted by the Bank of France's small interest rate cut on Thursday afternoon.
Bond futures finished pit-trading firmer too, tracking Bunds and other European debt markets higher after the U.S. market's rise overnight. A stronger U.S. opening helped support bonds.
The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.54, up 0.30. from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets slumped into the red in the afternoon session and stayed there to the close of trade, despite strength on Bunds and Treasuries. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.33, down 0.49 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened higher in quiet trade as foreign players returned to the market during the overnight session after a successful auction of inflation-indexed Treasury notes on Wednesday. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-14/32, up 6/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.88 percent.

JAPAN - Key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rebounded on Thursday after falls over the past two days, backed by the yen's rise against the dollar and losses for the Tokyo stock market. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.31, up 0.23 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - The primary market saw a ragbag of new issues Thursday morning with no one deal demanding particular attention.

French Groupe Danone's finance arm launched a $100 million three-year bond at a yield spread of 15 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The deal tightened to trade at 14/13 b.p. on broker screens shortly after breaking syndicate.
